Nashville Statement
NASH-vil STAYT-mint
noun phrase (document)
Named for Nashville, Tennessee, where it was adopted in August 2017 at a meeting of the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood (CBMW) held in conjunction with the annual conference of the Ethics and Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Nashville Statement (August 2017) is an evangelical confessional statement on biblical sexuality, marriage, and gender, drafted under the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood and signed by a broad coalition of evangelical leaders. Composed of a preamble and fourteen articles, each in the "We affirm... We deny..." form of a confessional statement, it sets out the historic Christian doctrine of human sexuality against the sexual revolution and the transgender movement. Its affirmations include: that God created man as male and female, two distinct and complementary sexes (Article 1); that the marriage covenant is between one man and one woman (Article 1); that the differences between male and female are part of God's good creational design (Article 4); that those who experience same-sex attraction or gender incongruity may live faithful Christian lives by walking in obedience (Articles 7-8); and, in its most controversial article (Article 10), that it is sinful to approve of homosexual immorality or transgenderism, and that such approval constitutes a departure from Christian faithfulness. The statement was a confessional line drawn at a cultural moment: a public, signed declaration that the historic biblical sexual ethic is not negotiable and that affirming theology (the dictionary's affirming-theology entry) is a departure from the faith. From the Reformed and complementarian standpoint the dictionary holds, the Nashville Statement is a faithful confessional response to the specific errors of its moment, anchored in the creational order of Genesis 1-2 and the apostolic sexual ethic. It was attacked from the progressive side as harsh and exclusionary, and criticized from some conservative quarters for not going far enough; the dictionary commends its substance while noting that a signature on a statement is the beginning, not the end, of faithfulness.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Evangelical confessional statement on biblical sexuality, marriage, and gender (August 2017, CBMW); fourteen affirm/deny articles upholding the historic Christian sexual ethic against the sexual revolution and transgenderism; Article 10 names approval of homosexual immorality and transgenderism as a departure from the faith.

Matthew 19:4-6 — "Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female... they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The Nashville Statement is corrupted when caricatured by progressives as cruelty toward sexual minorities, when a signature on it is mistaken for the substance of faithfulness, or when it is wielded as a tribal-loyalty test rather than received as a confession of the biblical sexual ethic.

expand to see more

Progressive caricature. The statement was widely attacked, on its release, as harsh, exclusionary, and harmful to LGBTQ persons. The caricature reads the document's clear denials as cruelty and its refusal to affirm as hatred. The statement itself, in Articles 7-8 and elsewhere, explicitly affirms the dignity of those who experience same-sex attraction or gender incongruity, calls the church to compassion, and holds out the gospel of transformation (1 Cor 6:11, "such were some of you: but ye are washed"). Naming sin as sin is not cruelty; it is the precondition of the gospel's offer of cleansing. The caricature mistakes clarity for cruelty and faithfulness for hatred.

Signature-as-faithfulness misreading. Adam Johns's own blog work tracking the later trajectories of confessional-statement signers makes the point sharply: a signature on the Nashville Statement (or the Dallas Statement, or the Danvers Statement) is the beginning of faithfulness, not its substance. Some who signed have since drifted; some who never signed have stood firm. The statement is a faithful confession of the biblical sexual ethic; subscribing it is good, but the test of a man is the settled trajectory of his life and ministry, not his name on a document. The dictionary commends the statement's substance while refusing to make a signature a sufficient measure of a man.
